abstract: Lipid homeostasis is essential for organismal function, as its disruption drives various metabolic disorders. Using an unbiased genetic modifier screen in Drosophila, we identified GAR1, a core component of the box H/ACA small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein complex, as a key regulator of systemic lipid storage. H/ACA small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein dysfunction reduces lipid droplet size in the fat body cells and promotes ectopic fat accumulation in the salivary gland cells. Null mutants of Gar1, Nop60B, and Nop10 display severe developmental defects, including reduced body size and larval lethality, whereas NHP2 null mutants die at the embryonic stage, indicating that this complex is critical for normal development. RNA-seq analysis, followed by RT-PCR validation, revealed that Gar1 dysfunction perturbs the splicing of sgg, which encodes a key regulator of insulin signaling. Consistently, knockdown of Gar1 or Nop60B impaired PI3K/AKT signaling, as evidenced by reduced membrane localization of the tGPH, a GFP reporter for PIP3 in the salivary gland cells. Notably, overexpression of Akt suppressed the reduction in lipid storage in Gar1-silenced flies. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized link between the H/ACA small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein complex and metabolic processes, such as lipid storage and development, and support the role of this complex as a regulator that may be functionally linked to insulin signaling.
